target.name: STATE OF MAHARASHTRA v. TAPAS D. NEOGY

plain: No overruling or doubt was found in the later judgments we hold that cite this case. That is silence in what we hold, not a finding that it is good law: see the coverage block.

recent_approving.sentence: It follows from the aforesaid discussion that the decision in Tapas D. Neogy [State of Maharashtra v. Tapas D. Neogy, (1999) 7 SCC 685 : 1999 SCC (Cri) 1352] did not go into and decide the issue: whether immovable property would fall under the expression “any property” under Section 102 of the Code.
recent_approving.prev: The test was affirmed by a three-Judge Bench of this Court in Nevada Properties (P) Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra reported in (2019) 20 SCC 119 wherein it was held thus: “13.
recent_approving.next: We say so by applying the inversion test as referred to in State of Gujarat v. Utility Users’ Welfare Assn. [State of Gujarat v. Utility Users’ Welfare Assn., (2018) 6 SCC 21] , which states that the Court must first carefully frame the supposed proposition 834  [2025] 7 S.C.R. Supreme Court Reports of law and then insert in the proposition a word reversing its meaning to get the answer whether or not a decision is a precedent for that proposition.

limits: Triage is a reading aid made by pattern rules over the sentences that name the case; it is not legal advice and not a verdict.
Only Supreme Court judgments we hold are searched; High Court treatment and judgments we lack are invisible.
Each quoted sentence was checked word for word against the judgment's text; the reading of it is a rule's, so a person must confirm.
